To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the superposition of edge creation processes to a node under uniform selection in heterogeneous dynamic graphs converges to a renewal process, which is a Poisson process with a time-dependent rate, and (2) the rate of the renewal process is a function of the node's out-degree and the time elapsed since the node's last arrival or departure, which is determined by the node lifetime distribution, the node's out-degrees, and the edge-arrival process.
the superposition of edge processes in dynamic graphs converges to a renewal process when the number of nodes in the network becomes sufficiently large.
the superposition of heterogeneous point processes in dynamic networks with churn converges to Poisson when system size becomes large.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: How does a superposition of heterogeneous point processes in a dynamic random graph with node churn converge to a Poisson point process?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a superposition of heterogeneous and dependent node arrival processes to a live (i.e., active) node converges to a renewal point process with the same intensity as the superposition of the node failure processes.

a superposition of heterogeneous node arrival processes in dynamic random graph converges to a homogeneous Poisson process when the system size is large enough, which is a fundamental result for future modeling of dynamic networks with churn.

the superposition of edge arrival processes to a live (active) node under uniform selection, in a dynamic graph with arbitrary node lifetimes, initial degree distributions, edge creation processes, and edge dependency, converges to a homogeneous Poisson process with intensity equal to the average edge arrival rate to a live node.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, despite the complex dependency of the edge creation processes and non-renewable nature of the arrival processes of both initial and replaced edges, the superposition of edge arrival processes to a live nodes converges to a homogeneous Poisson process when the system size is sufficiently large.
the superposition of heterogeneous point processes in dynamic random networks can be approximated by a Poisson process as the system size becomes sufficiently larger.
we prove that the edge creation process in dynamic graphs can be approximated by Poisson process, and the approximation is valid for both regular and irregular graphs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Poisson process can be applied as a building block for modeling the superposition of heterogeneous node arrival and failure processes in dynamic random networks.

, despite a large number of heterogeneous edge-arrival processes in a dynamic random graph with node churn, a superposition process of edge-arrivals to a live node still converges to a renewal Poisson process when the number of active nodes in the system becomes large.

the superposition of heterogeneous point processes in a large-scale dynamic random graph can still be well-approximated by a Poisson process, which is the cornerstone of our proposed modeling approach.
